references.text: The elders of Moab are mentioned here together with the elders of Midian, showing the alliance between these two groups against Israel.
Balaam is later killed along with the kings of Midian, linking him to both Moab and Midian.
Divination (קְסָמִים) was forbidden in Israel, and this shows that Moab and Midian used pagan practices.
Balaam is called a prophet here, confirming his connection to divination.
Ezekiel condemns divination, the same practice brought by the elders of Moab and Midian.
The teaching of Balaam is mentioned as a warning, referring back to the events with Balak.
Balaam's error is cited as an example of false teaching for profit.
The teaching of Balaam and Balak are mentioned together as a warning against false teaching in the church.
